Description

2022 Topps Chrome was released September 16th. Each Hobby box will yield two autographs, eight inserts and 12 Refractors while each Jumbo box will have five autos and twelve Refractors.

Despite being released near the conclusion of the 2022 season, many players are depicted in their 2021 uniforms.

We estimate that around 96,000 Hobby boxes were produced, and increase of 20% over last year's product.

Sonic

On February 24th, 2023, Topps released 2022 Topps Chrome Sonic. Sonic is a re-release of the entire 225-card 2022 Topps Chrome base set, but with new parallels and inserts. And yes, despite being released at around the same time as 2023 Spring Training, players are still depicted with their 2021 teams.

MVP Buyback Promotion

As a way to clear out the excessive amount of unsold Topps Chrome wax, and to make amends for the high-number short-print (see below) debacle, on November 23rd Topps announced the "MVP Buyback" promotion. Beginning November 26th, and continuing until March 30th, 2023, collectors can turn in base cards, Gimmicks, and Refractors of Aaron Judge and Paul Goldschmidt (the 2022 AL and NL MVPs) to participating Hobby stores and receive store credit. Collectors will receive the following for each card surrendered.

  • $20 for each base and Gimmick card.
  • $40 for each un-numbered Refractor.
  • $100 for each Refractor serial-numbered to 100 copies or greater.
  • $200 for each Refractor serial-numbered to 100 copies or fewer.

This promotion also includes cards from the 2022 Topps Chrome Logofractor and 2022 Topps Chrome Sonic sets.

Distribution

Hobby: 24 packs per box, four cards per pack. 12 boxes per case.

Jumbo: 12 packs per box, 13 cards per pack. Eight boxes per case.

Sonic: 16 packs per box, four cards per pack. 16 boxes per case.

High-Number Short Prints

NOTE: The five "high-number" cards (#221-225) were added late to the production run; however, these cards were never included in packs. On September 19th -- three days after the release of Chrome -- Topps posted a statement to their Facebook page blaming a "technical miscommunication" with their printing subcontractor for the absence of these cards in packs.

Topps announced that these cards will be randomly inserted into special four-card "Silver Packs" that will be distributed to Hobby dealers, Hobby distributors, group breakers, and those who purchased Hobby boxes directly from topps.com at the rate of one Silver Pack for each Hobby box ordered. In addition, Hobby LITE boxes, which were exclusive to topps.com, will have the High-Number Short Prints. Topps Chrome Sonic, released in February 2023, also had the five cards.

Topps began fulfilling the first wave of Silver Packs in early October. These packs contain a variety of 2022 Topps Chrome base, Refractor parallel, and insert cards as well as autographs from various Topps products that originally packed out as redemption cards, but were never redeemed. We estimate that the odds of finding a High-Number Short Print in a Silver pack to be around 1:20. In addition, all of the "base" High-Number Short Prints are Refractors.

  • 221 Bobby Witt, Jr.
  • 222 Julio Rodriguez
  • 223 Spencer Torkelson
  • 224 Hunter Greene
  • 225 CJ Abrams

Sonic

Topps released 2022 Topps Chrome Sonic on February, 2023, and at first glance, it appears that all 225 base cards are identical to those from the standard Topps Chrome released. While there is no obvious determinant, for the Sonic edition, the Topps Chrome logo on the front is on the opposite side of the card. Also, where appropriate, the "RC" icon is also on the opposite side of the card and slightly larger on the Sonic cards. That, and each Sonic base card has a production code ending in 439, whereas the standard Chrome cards have a production code ending in 967.

We estimate 49,975 copies of each Sonic base card were produced.

The following parallels are exclusive to Sonic packs, and includes all 225 base cards -- including the five high-number short prints.

  • Green RayWave Refractors (serial-numbered to 99 copies)
  • Gold RayWave Refractors (serial-numbered to 50 copies)
  • Orange/Black Sonic Pulse Refractors (serial-numbered to 25 copies)
  • Red/Black Sonic Pulse Refractors (serial-numbered to five)

In addition, the first 220 base cards are available in the following Refractor parallels.

  • Refractors
  • Prism Refractors
  • Black & White RayWave Refractors
  • Purple/Yellow Sonic Refractors (serial-numbered to 299 copies)
  • Aqua RayWave Refractors (serial-numbered to 199 copies)
  • Aqua/Pink Sonic Refractors (serial-numbered to 199 copies)
  • Green/Yellow Sonic Refractors (serial-numbered to 99 copies)
  • Blue/Yellow Sonic Refractors (serial-numbered to 75 copies)
  • Red RayWave Refractors (serial-numbered to five)

NOTE: As with the Sonic base set, the Topps Chrome logo is also flipped on the Refractor and Prism Refractor parallels, differentiating them from the Refractors and Prism Refractors inserted into standard Chrome packs.

We estimate the production figures for each Sonic Refractor parallel as such.

  • Sonic Refractor: 4875 copies
  • Sonic Black & White RayWave Refractor: 3675 copies
  • Sonic Prism Refractor: 2425 copies
